name: Low-latency object memory pool (MemPool)
listed_description: Template pool that pre-allocates a block of objects at construction and hands out and reclaims slots at runtime without calling the heap allocator on the hot path.
claim_text: Avoids dynamic memory allocation on the critical code path; book restates the cost of dynamic allocation but gives no numbers.
book_benchmark: None. Book shows only a small example program that allocates and frees doubles and a struct and prints addresses. Author environment: Linux 5.19, GCC 11.3.0, CMake 3.23.2, Ninja 1.10.2, release build.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 4, Designing C++ memory pools to avoid dynamic memory allocations (Handling deallocations, Using the memory pool with an example)

name: Lock-free SPSC queue (LFQueue)
listed_description: Single-producer single-consumer FIFO queue over a preallocated std::vector with two std::atomic indices; producer gets a pointer to the next slot, fills it, then publishes by bumping the write index.
claim_text: Locks and mutexes cause context switches that degrade critical threads tremendously; lock-free queue avoids locks and context switches.
book_benchmark: None. Book shows only a producer and consumer example program printing queue size. No latency or throughput numbers.
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 4, Transferring data using lock-free queues (Designing lock-free queue storage, Adding elements to the queue, Consuming elements from the queue)

name: Asynchronous low-latency logger (lock-free queue plus background writer thread)
listed_description: Logger where hot threads push typed log elements (char, ints, floats, strings) onto the SPSC lock-free queue and a separate thread formats and writes them to disk; log call cost is only pushing characters and values onto the queue.
claim_text: Only overhead of log() is iterating characters and pushing values onto the lock-free queue; disk I/O and slow string formatting moved off the hot thread.
book_benchmark: None. No timings. Book notes the char-by-char push could be replaced with a single memcpy as a possible improvement.
guessed_baseline: synchronous file logging (fprintf / std::ofstream / printf-style logger)
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 4, Building a low latency logging framework (Designing the low latency logger, Pushing data to the logger queue)

name: Non-blocking TCP socket and epoll server framework (TCPSocket, TCPServer)
listed_description: Socket wrapper with non-blocking mode, Nagle disabled (TCP_NODELAY) and a server that monitors sockets with edge-triggered epoll, plus send and receive buffers and callbacks.
claim_text: For low latency applications, disabling the latency associated with Nagle's algorithm sending packets out is imperative.
book_benchmark: None. Book runs a small TCP client and server example and shows log output; no latency numbers.
guessed_baseline: blocking sockets with Nagle enabled / level-triggered poll
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 4, C++ network programming using sockets (Disabling Nagle's algorithm, Adding and removing monitored sockets)

name: Pool-backed limit order book with array-indexed hash maps and intrusive linked lists
listed_description: Matching-engine order book: price levels in a doubly linked list per side, orders FIFO in a linked list per level, lookups through fixed-size std::array maps indexed by price, order id and client id, objects drawn from memory pools so no dynamic allocation or copying on the hot path.
claim_text: Data structures must avoid dynamic memory allocations and copy as little data as possible; efficient insert and remove of orders.
book_benchmark: None. Book runs exchange_main and shows start-up log lines only; no matching throughput or latency numbers.
guessed_baseline: std::map and std::unordered_map keyed order book with heap-allocated orders
found_in: book: Building Low Latency Applications with C++ (2023), ch. 6, Building the order book and matching orders (Building the internal data structures, Defining the MEOrder, OrderHashMap, and ClientOrderHashMap types)
